title: Learning piano tuning at Werlein's
summary: Learned tuning from piano technician Bill Reedy and books; arthritis forced him to quit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, after I started to work for Whirlions, how I learned it was at every spare moment of my time I would go into the tuning shop, into the repair shop of Whirlions. And I became very good friends with old man Bill Reedy, who was one of the finest piano technicians that I ever met in all my life and wouldn't tell anybody anything. But I'm the only one that he would let sit there because once in a while he loved his booze and I'd slip him a half a pint. And he thought the world of me, but he'd run the hell out of anybody else. And he didn't, I don't think that he knew at the time that I was watching him to learn his technique. And then I got books on it.
And have you ever taught anybody what you know?

No. Because it hasn't, the occasion hasn't come up because I just, I have sold all of my stock and everything. I still have my tuning tools, but I can't tune anymore on the kind of arthritis in my right hand. Doctor made me quit. See how it's all swollen there? It's just, it's down to almost normal, but you can see the difference in it. See, see the difference?

And when I do too much playing, especially jazz, then it begins to swell on me. So the doctor once told me, when he examined it, he said, Now, what's aggravating it is so much as the tuning wrench. There are two, on average of 227 strings on the piano. And to pull on that wrench, no matter how slightly, and you don't put big pressure on it. No matter how slight you think would average about five times on each pull, on each string. 227 times five is over nearly 12.

1100 times on one piano and I've tuned as many as five pianos on a day and the aggravation I just had to give it up or else just quit altogether both of them because it would have ruined me and I love the play. Must be Ellen.
